parts.label: a
parts.technique: Expectation E(X) of discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean of discrete random variables; explaining E(X)=2 relies on the excluded mean concept.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: The mark scheme allows the equation 3a+2b=1 to come from 'sum of probabilities = 1', an in-spec basic probability property, giving full marks without using E(X); alternative in-spec method available.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of variance of discrete random variables; this part requires forming an equation using Var(X)=7.1.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Solving simultaneous equations dependent on excluded variance equation
parts.reason: Depends on the equation from part (c), which is out of spec (variance calculation); part only makes sense after the out-of-spec part.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: E(Y) and Var(Y) of linear transformation of discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables; this explicitly requires E(Y) and Var(Y).

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Probability calculation dependent on excluded parts
parts.reason: Requires the values of a and b obtained from the excluded variance-based equations in (c)/(d), so this part only makes sense after out-of-spec parts.

parts.reason: These are the building blocks explicitly used for regression and correlation coefficient calculations, both of which are explicitly excluded (S2.2, S5.1); this preparatory calculation is inseparable from the excluded regression/correlation context.
